root_cause.text: In the Spacemit EMAC transmit path (`emac_tx_mem_map()`), the error-handling path failed to unwind previously DMA-mapped TX buffers when a mapping step returned an error, so the driver leaked DMA mappings in the TX ring.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a cleanup loop in `err_free_skb` that iterates from `old_head` to `head` and calls `emac_free_tx_buf(priv, i)` for each partially mapped TX buffer, and the commit message explicitly states “The DMA mappings were leaked on mapping error. Free them with the existing emac_free_tx_buf() function.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local loop/index variable to `emac_tx_mem_map()` for subsequent use.
intent_record.what: A new local variable `i` of type `u32` was added to the declaration list in `emac_tx_mem_map()`, changing `u32 head, old_head, frag_num, f;` to `u32 head, old_head, frag_num, f, i;`.
intent_record.how: This only affects the function's local scope by making an additional loop/index variable available for use later in the function; by itself it does not change runtime behavior until that variable is referenced elsewhere in the function body.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free partially allocated TX descriptors on transmit mapping failure to prevent TX ring resource leaks.
intent_record.what: In the tx mapping error path of emac_tx_mem_map(), after incrementing the TX dropped counter and before freeing the skb, a new loop was added that resets i to old_head and iterates until head, calling emac_free_tx_buf(priv, i) for each TX ring entry and wrapping i back to 0 when it reaches tx_ring->total_cnt.
intent_record.how: On a transmit mapping failure, the driver now releases any TX buffer descriptors that were already allocated during the partial mapping attempt, instead of leaving them owned by the ring. This prevents leaked TX resources and keeps the ring state consistent after an error.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable transmit mapping path is present in this snippet. In `emac_tx_mem_map()`, the code maps fragments in a loop and on error jumps to `err_free_skb:`: `if (emac_tx_map_frag(dev, &tx_desc, tx_buf, skb, f)) { ... goto err_free_skb; }`. The only unwind at that label is `dev_dstats_tx_dropped(priv->ndev); dev_kfree_skb_any(skb);` — there is no cleanup of any earlier successfully DMA-mapped TX buffers or descriptors in the ring. This matches the root cause: previously mapped TX buffers are not unwound when a later mapping step fails. The fix is not present because there is no call to unmap already-mapped descriptors/buffers in the error path, nor any rollback of `tx_ring->head` or per-buffer DMA state.
